label: Grandparent
summary: Each grandparent of the character.
details: Runs on a character.

label: Great-grandchild
summary: Each great-grandchild of the character.
details: Runs on a character. These are the children of the character's grandchildren.

label: Great-grandparent
summary: Each great-grandparent of the character.
details: Runs on a character. These are the parents of the character's grandparents.

label: Great project
summary: Each Great Project that is currently active anywhere in the game.
details: It needs no character or title to start from. Vanilla checks the project's owner, founder, type and location inside it, and uses the random form to pick a project and save it under a name.

label: Province great project
summary: Each active Great Project located in the province.
details: Runs on a province. Vanilla uses it only as a check, and every use has a group of OR conditions inside.

label: Great project type
summary: Each Great Project type defined in the game.
details: This walks through the kinds of project, not the projects themselves. Vanilla uses it once, to test which types a character can plan.

label: Guest subset
summary: Each character in one named group of guests of an activity, across its past, current and future phases.
details: Runs on an activity. A subset is a named group of guests that the activity sets up (vanilla uses names such as qualified, entrants, spectators and winner). With a phase given, only the groups of that phase are used.

fields.name: name
fields.text: The key of the guest group to go through.
fields.values: a subset key defined by the activity

fields.name: phase
fields.text: Only use the group as it exists in this phase of the activity.
fields.values: a phase key of the activity

label: Current-phase guest subset
summary: Each character in one named group of guests, looking only at the phase the activity is in right now.
details: Runs on an activity. It works like the guest subset list, but without a phase option: past and future phases are left out.

fields.name: name
fields.text: The key of the guest group to go through.
fields.values: a subset key defined by the activity

label: Hegemony
summary: Each hegemony in the game, given as its title.
details: It needs no starting point. Each item is a title; vanilla looks at the holder of that title inside it.

label: Heir
summary: Each character who is first in line to inherit one of the character's held titles.
details: Runs on a character. Vanilla uses it to flag or give traits to the heirs and to pick a new governor.

label: Heir title
summary: Each title the character is heir to.
details: Runs on a character. Vanilla sorts these by the character's place in the line of succession and often checks the title's holder or tier.

label: Held title
summary: Each landed title the character holds.
details: Runs on a character. Vanilla uses it with titles from barony up to empire. You can limit it to a tier.

fields.name: title_tier
fields.text: Only go through titles of this tier. A comparison such as `>= county` also works.
fields.values: barony, county, duchy, kingdom, empire, or a comparison

label: Hired mercenary company
summary: Each mercenary company the character has hired.
details: Runs on a character. Vanilla uses it once, in a check with `always = yes`.

label: Holding type
summary: Each holding type defined in the game.
details: This walks through the kinds of holding, not through actual holdings.

label: Holy site
summary: Each active holy site of the faith.
details: Runs on a faith. You can limit it to the eminent holy sites or to the others. For eminent ones the game says to prefer its own eminent holy site list.

fields.name: is_eminent
fields.text: yes goes through only eminent holy sites, no only the non-eminent ones. Leave it out to go through all.

label: Holy site barony
summary: Each barony that is an active holy site of the faith.
details: Runs on a faith. Vanilla often counts them or checks who holds the county they are in.

label: Enshrined artifact
summary: Each artifact that is enshrined in the holy site.
details: Runs on a holy site. Vanilla checks whether each is a holy relic of a faith and sets its owner.

label: Holy site faith
summary: Each faith that counts the holy site as one of its own.
details: Runs on a holy site. The wording of the game's documentation means a site can belong to several faiths.

label: Holy site type
summary: Each holy site type defined in the game.
details: This walks through the kinds of holy site, not through the sites.

label: Home court hostage
summary: Each hostage who is currently held abroad.
details: Going by its name, these are hostages from the character's home court. Vanilla compares their warden with a saved court owner (the warden is the ruler who keeps them, going by its use). The game's documentation does not say whose hostages are meant.

label: Hooked character
summary: Each character the character has a hook on.
details: Runs on a character. A hook is a hold over another character that can be used to demand a favour.

label: Hostile raider
summary: Each character the character is hostile to because their top liege's realm was raided.
details: Runs on a character. Vanilla uses it only as a check, comparing the entries with an army owner.

label: House claimed artifact
summary: Each artifact the house has claimed.
details: Runs on a dynasty house. Vanilla uses it to save an artifact, to add artifacts to a list and, in one place, on the house of a saved attacker.

label: House member
summary: Each member of the dynasty house.
details: Runs on a dynasty house. Vanilla uses it to give opinions, add members to lists, pick the house head and count members with a modifier. The game does not say whether dead members are included.

label: House relation
summary: Each relation the house has with another house.
details: Runs on a dynasty house. Vanilla checks the relation level and its parameters, and reaches the other house with the relation house lists inside it.

label: House unity member
summary: Each character that counts as a valid member for the house's unity.
details: Runs on a dynasty house. The game does not say what makes a member valid. Vanilla uses it to pick or count available adults.

label: Important location
summary: Each county that is important for at least one title.
details: It needs no starting point. The game does not explain what makes a county important and vanilla does not use it.

label: Important location for the title
summary: Each county that is important for the title.
details: Runs on a title. The game does not explain what makes a county important and vanilla does not use it.

label: Title in the de facto hierarchy
summary: The title itself, its actual vassal titles, and the titles below them.
details: Runs on a title. De facto means by who holds what now, not by the map's borders. A `continue` block decides whether to go down further from each title. It is separate from `limit`: a title that fails the limit is left out of the list, but its vassals are still visited as long as `continue` allows.

fields.name: continue
fields.text: Conditions deciding whether to go on to a title's own vassals.

label: Title in the de jure hierarchy
summary: The title itself, the titles that belong under it by the map, and the titles below those.
details: Runs on a title. De jure means by the map's fixed borders, whoever holds the land. A `continue` block decides whether to go down further from each title. It is separate from `limit`: a title that fails the limit is left out of the list, but its vassals are still visited as long as `continue` allows.

fields.name: continue
fields.text: Conditions deciding whether to go on to a title's own de jure vassals.

label: Item in a global list
summary: Each item stored in a global list.
details: The game's documentation says to name the list with `list` or `variable`, but vanilla always uses `variable = <list name>` here, so write that. Global lists are shared across the whole game.

fields.name: variable
fields.text: The name of the global list to go through.

fields.name: list
fields.text: The game's documentation names this as another way to give the list. Vanilla does not use it here.

label: Item in a list
summary: Each item saved in a named list.
details: Items usually get into a list with `add_to_list` earlier in the script. The items can be characters, titles or anything else that was added. Vanilla mostly names the list with `list`; `variable` is used for lists kept as variables.

fields.name: list
fields.text: The name of the list to go through.

fields.name: variable
fields.text: The name of a variable list to go through instead.

label: Item in a local list
summary: Each item stored in a local list.
details: The game says nothing more than its documentation, which names the list with `list` or `variable`. Vanilla does not use it, so how it differs from the plain list is not known.

fields.name: list
fields.text: The name of the local list.

fields.name: variable
fields.text: The name of a variable list instead.

label: Independent ruler
summary: Each independent ruler in the game who holds land and whose highest title is a county or above.
details: It needs no starting point. Vanilla uses it to give opinions, build lists and start events.

label: Infected province
summary: Each province the epidemic has infected.
details: Runs on an epidemic. Vanilla checks the county and its holder, and the distance to a place.

label: Inspiration
summary: Each inspiration in the world.
details: It needs no starting point. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Inspired character
summary: Each character who currently has an inspiration.
details: It needs no starting point. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Interested title
summary: Each title that is interested in any county.
details: It needs no starting point. The game does not say what interested means here, and vanilla does not use it.

label: Interloper ruler
summary: Each character who is an interloper in the struggle.
details: Runs on a struggle. Vanilla uses it to give opinions and fire events.

label: Intrigue councillor
summary: Each of the character's councillors in an intrigue-based post.
details: Runs on a character. The game's documentation is short and does not name the posts, so which councillors count is left to the game.

label: Invited activity
summary: Each activity the character has been invited to.
details: Runs on a character. Vanilla uses it only as a check, comparing the entries with a saved activity.

label: Invited character
summary: Each character who has been invited to the activity and has not answered yet.
details: Runs on an activity. Once a guest accepts or declines, they leave the list.

label: Involved county
summary: Each county that is involved in the struggle.
details: Runs on a struggle. Vanilla uses it with a limit and then acts inside it.

label: Involved ruler
summary: Each character who is involved in the struggle.
details: Runs on a struggle. Vanilla uses it to give opinions, add the rulers to lists, and to test whether they are their own top liege, hold a primary title or are landed.

label: Killed character
summary: Each character the character has killed.
details: The game's scope list also names artifacts as a place this can run, but the game's documentation does not say what that means. Vanilla checks the death reason or sorts by days since death.

label: Kingdom
summary: Each kingdom title in the game.
details: It needs no starting point. Vanilla uses it to build lists of possible targets and to look at the holders, and sometimes checks that a holder exists first.

label: Knight
summary: Each knight of the character.
details: Runs on a character. Vanilla uses it a lot to add knights to lists, give opinions and rank them by prowess, martial skill or age, and in places checks whether a knight is landed or picks a new employer for one.

label: Known innovation
summary: Each innovation the culture already knows.
details: Runs on a culture. Vanilla uses it to find an innovation that meets a condition.

label: Known secret
summary: Each secret the character knows about.
details: Runs on a character. It includes secrets of other people, not only the character's own. Vanilla checks who owns the secret, who it is about and what type it is.

label: Neighboring realm
summary: Each realm bordering the realm of the character's top liege, given as its top title, if its top liege is someone else.
details: Runs on a character. Land borders that tributaries add also count. The border data can be a day or two out of date. Vanilla does not use it.
